accepted.notes: Structure verified (6 sequential calls/market in descriptors, 4-5/market in YB, multicall3 proven at line 436) and the fix is behavior-preserving. finding.title: crvUSD market discovery issues ~6 sequential eth_calls per market instead of one multicall batch
finding.description: fetchLlammaMarketDescriptors (lines 343-381) makes 6 individual HTTP eth_call requests per LLAMMA market (collaterals/controllers/amms + symbol/min_band/max_band) at concurrency 2, and fetchYieldBasisMarketPositions (lines 517-564) makes 4-5 more per Yield Basis market — on the order of 150-250 HTTP round-trips per cron run for a few dozen markets. The sequential discovery leg also raises the odds the optional Yield Basis 6s timeout (YIELD_BASIS_OPTIONAL_TIMEOUT_MS, line 118) fires as market count grows, spuriously degrading the snapshot, and it contends with the shared per-trigger connection pool and adapter IO limiter.

Same contracts, same selectors, same decoded values — outputs are byte-identical, so it is behavior-preserving. preview_emergency_withdraw with a custom gas limit can stay as an individual call.
finding.estImpact: removes ~150-250 RPC round-trips per cron run

accepted.notes: Verified: release() decrements active and resolves the waiter synchronously, but the waiter's `active += 1` (line 79) runs on a later microtask; an independent already-queued microtask calling run() in between observes active<max and starts, yielding max+1 concurrency plus queue-jumping. Realistic with multiple adapters sharing the limiter. Low severity appropriate.

finding.title: Adapter IO limiter can exceed maxParallel: released slot is stealable before the queued waiter resumes
finding.description: release() decrements `active` and then resolves the next queued waiter, but the waiter only re-increments `active` inside run() after its promise continuation executes on a later microtask (lines 72-85). A new run() call that arrives between the synchronous decrement and the waiter's resumption observes active < max, skips the queue, and starts immediately; when the waiter then resumes, active becomes max+1. Concrete scenario with max=2: A and B running, C queued; A finishes → active=1, C resolved; D calls run() before C's continuation executes → active=2, D runs; C resumes → active=3. Three concurrent IOs despite RESERVE_ADAPTER_MAX_PARALLEL_IO=2 — this is the limiter meant to keep reserve adapters inside Cloudflare's per-trigger 6-connection pool. Also causes queue-jumping (D ran before queued C conceptually).
finding.recommendation: Hand the slot off instead of freeing it: when release() finds a live waiter, resolve it without decrementing `active` (and have the waiter skip its own increment), or increment `active` on behalf of the waiter before resolving. This only tightens the limit to its documented value; callers see no behavioral difference beyond scheduling.
finding.estImpact: caps parallel IO at the intended 2, not 3+

remediation.summary: Changed the reserve adapter IO limiter to hand an occupied slot directly to the queued waiter instead of briefly decrementing the active count, preventing later callers from stealing the slot before the waiter resumes. Added a regression test covering the queue-jump microtask race.

accepted.notes: Verified: lines 91, 133, 186 all key on JSON.stringify(options?.headers ?? null) with headers typed HeadersInit (line 40). A Headers instance stringifies to "{}" (and would also break the `...spread` merge). Correctly framed as latent — current call sites pass plain objects. Low severity, cheap type-narrowing fix.

finding.title: Request-cache keys JSON.stringify HeadersInit, so Headers instances or entry arrays can collide
finding.description: fetchJsonWithRetry, fetchJsonPostWithRetry, and fetchTextWithRetry build their per-run dedup cache key with JSON.stringify(options?.headers ?? null) (lines 91, 133, 186). The parameter type is HeadersInit, which admits a Headers instance (stringifies to "{}") and a [string,string][] entries array as well as a plain record. If any future adapter passes a Headers object, two requests to the same URL with different headers would share one cache entry and the second caller would silently receive the first response (e.g. wrong Origin/Referer variant for CORS-gated issuer dashboards). Today every in-scope call site passes a plain object literal, so this is a latent boundary hazard rather than a live bug — hence medium confidence on impact.
finding.recommendation: Normalize before keying: convert HeadersInit to a sorted lowercase-key record (new Headers(init) then [...entries()].sort()) and stringify that, or narrow the option type to Record<string,string> so the compiler rejects Headers/entry-array inputs. Either change keeps all current cache keys stable for existing plain-object call sites.
finding.estImpact: closes a latent cross-request cache-collision hole

remediation.summary: Normalized non-record HeadersInit values into deterministic sorted header entries before request-cache serialization, while preserving the existing plain-record cache-key shape. Merged Headers and entry-array overrides through the Headers API so they are also sent correctly.

accepted.notes: All four legs verified: process-pools.ts:159 multi-attributes; run-shared knownPoolIds (orchestrator:223, staged-pool.ts:75, three crawl skip sites) makes later coins record poolsFound=0 (persistence.ts:166-174 increments misses); staging PK is (pool_id, stablecoin_id) so both rows can coexist across runs; SELECT at 242-256 has no ORDER BY and identity dedup ignores stablecoinId, so the winner is row-order dependent.

finding.title: Staged pools shared by two tracked coins are credited to only one coin, nondeterministically
finding.description: The DL primary path credits a pool to EVERY matched tracked coin (process-pools.ts:159 `for (const id of matchedIds)`), but the staged path enforces one-coin-per-pool twice: (a) during discovery, `context.addPool()` adds the raw poolId to the run-shared `knownPoolIds` set (staged-pool.ts:75), so when coin B is crawled after coin A in the same run, their shared pool is skipped for B (crawl-coingecko-pools.ts:118, crawl-geckoterminal-pools.ts:123, crawl-dexscreener-pools.ts:144) and B records poolsFound=0, incrementing consecutive_misses toward dormant; (b) in mergeStagedPools, the pool identity contains no stablecoinId, so when rows (pool,A) and (pool,B) both exist in staging (created across runs), the second row hit by the un-ORDERed SELECT (line 244) is dropped as duplicate_exact_identity (lines 404-432). Which coin wins depends on row return order, so a shared pool's TVL can flip between coins across runs.
finding.recommendation: Decide the intended semantics explicitly. If staged pools should match the DL multi-attribution semantics, key staged-vs-staged dedup per stablecoin (include stablecoinId in the exact key for that comparison while keeping global keys for staged-vs-DL/direct dedup) and drop the cross-coin knownPoolIds skip in discovery (tickers already namespace by coin). At minimum add ORDER BY to the staging SELECT so the winner is deterministic. Fixing attribution changes liquidity figures for affected coins (behaviorChange=true); the evidence it is wrong today is the direct inconsistency with the primary-path semantics plus the discovery-side false miss that can demote a coin to dormant despite a live pool.
finding.estImpact: stable coverage for small stables sharing pools; no false dormant demotions

remediation.summary: Namespaced discovery-time known-pool suppression by stablecoin and changed staged merge dedupe so primary/direct known pools remain globally deduped while accepted staged rows dedupe per stablecoin. Shared staged pools can now be credited to each tracked coin, matching primary-path multi-attribution, while accepted identities still flow back into the global fallback dedupe index.

accepted.notes: Code matches (sync-config.ts:359-374; scanTo=min(from+range-1,head) so events branch can pass head-margin). But 'every cron re-issues the same ranges' is wrong: the next empty run advances via full-success-empty, so redundancy is one bounded overlap window per event batch, and configs rotate. Real, safe fix (INSERT OR IGNORE confirmed), modest impact.

finding.title: Mint-burn scan watermark under-advances after successful runs with events, re-scanning covered ranges
finding.description: On full success, the empty-result branch advances the watermark to min(scanTo, chainHead - safetyMarginBlocks), but the with-events branch sets newLastBlock = summary.maxBlockSeen (the newest persisted row's block). Everything in (maxBlockSeen, scanTo] was fully scanned with complete event coverage, zero missing timestamps, and zero tx-context shortfalls, yet is re-fetched next run. For sparse-activity contracts whose last event is tens of thousands of blocks behind head, every cron re-issues the same empty Alchemy getLogs ranges (chunked calls per event def), burning the per-config request budget. The branch is also asymmetric on reorg safety: it can advance past chainHead - safetyMargin when an event lands inside the margin, so the margin isn't the reason for the conservatism.
finding.recommendation: In the full-success-events branch, advance to Math.max(summary.maxBlockSeen, Math.min(scanTo, chainHead - safetyMarginBlocks)). Behavior-preserving: re-scanned ranges are known-empty (and inserts are dedup'd via INSERT-ignore); only redundant Alchemy calls disappear.
finding.estImpact: saves up to dozens of Alchemy getLogs calls per cron run

remediation.summary: Advanced successful mint/burn scans with events to the safe scan frontier instead of stopping at the newest persisted event block, eliminating one bounded re-scan window for known-empty covered blocks.
remediation.notes: The event branch still preserves the newest event block when it is ahead of the safe frontier; partial coverage, missing timestamps, and deferred tx-context branches keep their existing frontier caps.

finding.title: recoveryPriceMode dual-statement close-event persistence is redundant
finding.description: close-event commands carry both recoveryPrice and a recoveryPriceMode discriminator ("bind" | "null"), and persistence branches into two nearly identical UPDATE statements — one hardcoding `recovery_price = NULL`, one binding the value. Every emitter with mode "null" (decision-engine.ts:337/491, repair.ts:100/134) also sets recoveryPrice: null, and every "bind" emitter passes a non-null number, so binding command.recoveryPrice in a single statement produces identical SQL semantics in all cases (binding null writes NULL). The mode field and the branch add a discriminator across 4 files that encodes nothing the value doesn't already say.

finding.estImpact: -15 LOC across 4 files

remediation.summary: Removed the redundant recoveryPriceMode discriminator from depeg close-event commands and collapsed persistence to one UPDATE that binds recoveryPrice, relying on null binding to write SQL NULL.

finding.title: Telegram dispatch records a circuit failure on abort and non-Telegram (D1) errors
finding.description: The catch-all at dispatch-telegram-alerts.ts:1042-1045 runs `recordOutcome(db, CIRCUIT_SOURCE.TELEGRAM_API, false)` for ANY error thrown in the try block — including AbortError from `throwIfAborted(signal)` (lines 858/873/544; the signal is the scheduled-runner cron-timeout signal, see handlers/scheduled/five-minute-telegram.ts:110) and D1 failures in `loadDispatchSourceData`/`buildDispatchSnapshotState` before any Telegram API call is made. `recordOutcome(false)` increments consecutiveFailures and opens the circuit at CIRCUIT_OPEN_THRESHOLD (circuit-breaker.ts:297-306). Repeated soft-deadline aborts or a D1 blip can therefore open the TELEGRAM_API circuit and suppress fresh alert fanout even though Telegram itself is healthy. The codebase convention elsewhere is to rethrow on abort WITHOUT recording an outcome (sync-fx-rates-helpers.ts:99, sync-kinesis-supply.ts:114). discovery-scan.ts:177-180 has the same abort-counts-as-CG-failure pattern in miniature.
finding.recommendation: In the catch block, skip recordOutcome when `signal?.aborted` (or the error is an AbortError) and rethrow, matching the sync-fx-rates-helpers convention. Ideally only record a Telegram failure for errors raised after Telegram interaction begins (drain/delivery), not for source-loading D1 errors. This only corrects internal circuit bookkeeping; no published figures, API shapes, or message content change.
finding.estImpact: prevents false circuit-opens that suppress live alerts

remediation.summary: Changed Telegram dispatch failure recording so aborts and pre-delivery source/D1 failures no longer increment the Telegram API circuit. Delivery-start tracking is marked immediately before non-empty pending, overflow, or subscriber send batches, with regressions for pre-delivery abort and source-load failure.

finding.title: USD-only TREASURY_RATES circuit gates all 12 currency benchmarks in fetch-tbill-rate
finding.description: The CIRCUIT_SOURCE.TREASURY_RATES breaker is fed exclusively by the USD source outcome (lines 739-743: FRED DGS3MO / Treasury XML success or failure), yet the circuit-open branch at line 693 short-circuits the ENTIRE run: EUR/CHF/GBP/JPY/AUD/MXN/BRL/CAD/RUB/TRY/USD_EFFR providers (ECB, SIX, FRED-SONIA, BoJ, RBA, Banxico, BCB, BoC, CBR, CBRT) are never attempted and every benchmark is forced to `buildRetainedBenchmark(..., "circuit-open")` (lines 697-705). A FRED/Treasury outage lasting CIRCUIT_OPEN_THRESHOLD runs thus freezes all non-USD risk-free rates at stale retained values and advances the GBP retained-fallback alert streak, even though those central-bank sources are healthy and independently reachable. Their per-provider failures are already handled per-key via retained fallbacks, so the whole-run gate adds no protection for them.
finding.recommendation: Scope the circuit-open branch to the USD benchmark only: on open circuit, use the retained/hardcoded USD benchmark but still run the BENCHMARK_PROVIDER_ORDER loop for the other keys. If the whole-run gate was a deliberate cost-bounding decision, record success/failure per provider family instead of only the USD outcome so the gate reflects what it actually protects. Flagging behaviorChange because the fix restores fresh non-USD rates during USD-source outages (evidence: fallbackMode metadata reports "circuit-open" for currencies whose providers were never consulted).
finding.estImpact: keeps 11 currency benchmarks live during USD-source outages

remediation.summary: Scoped the TREASURY_RATES circuit-open path to the USD benchmark only. The branch now retains or hardcodes USD while continuing to resolve the non-USD benchmark provider order, using the same registry and degradation-reason helpers as the normal path.

finding.title: sync-kinesis-supply reports status "error" when chains are merely circuit-open skipped
finding.description: The status derivation `synced === total ? "ok" : synced > 0 ? "degraded" : "error"` (line 157) folds `skipped` (circuit-breaker deliberately open, lines 88-92) into the failure denominator. If both KAU and KAG circuits are open, the run performs zero work and zero failures yet returns status "error" — the strongest failure signal — even though the breaker skip is the intended protective behavior. Every other cron in this directory reports circuit-open skips as "degraded" (e.g. sync-bluechip.ts:108, sync-usds-status.ts:91, fetch-tbill-rate.ts:715) or tolerates them (sync-blacklist providerCircuitSkips -> degraded, line 511-512). The misclassification feeds cron-run history and failure-oriented watchdogs with a phantom hard error during a routine breaker window.
finding.recommendation: Derive status from actual failures: `failed === 0 ? (skipped > 0 ? "degraded" : "ok") : synced > 0 ? "degraded" : "error"`. Metadata already carries synced/failed/skipped so no shape change; only the status word for the circuit-open-only case changes, aligning it with the sibling jobs' established semantics.
finding.estImpact: removes phantom hard-error runs during breaker windows

remediation.summary: Changed sync-kinesis-supply status derivation to report skip-only circuit-open runs as degraded rather than error, while preserving error for genuine all-failed runs and existing synced/failed/skipped metadata.

accepted.notes: Verified: streamError break at line 72 exits with only releaseLock in finally, no cancel/drain. finding.title: Anthropic SSE stream error path abandons the response body without cancelling it
finding.description: When a mid-stream `error` event is seen, accumulateAnthropicStream breaks out of the read loop (lines 66-73) and only calls reader.releaseLock() in the finally block — it never cancels the reader or drains the remaining body. On Cloudflare Workers an unconsumed response body keeps the subrequest connection occupied, and this repo's hard rule is that cron jobs must consume response bodies before opening more fetches (the digest chain shares the 08:05 slot's 6-connection pool with sync-bluechip, and requestDigestCopy may immediately re-fetch for the corrective retry). The success path fully consumes the stream, so only the error path leaks.
finding.recommendation: In the streamError break path (or in finally when the loop exited early), call `await reader.cancel().catch(() => {})` before releaseLock. Cancelling signals CF to reclaim the connection; thrown error and all parsing behavior are unchanged.
finding.estImpact: frees a pooled connection on stream errors in the digest slot

remediation.summary: Cancelled the Anthropic SSE reader when a stream error exits before EOF, while preserving the thrown error and normal EOF handling.
remediation.notes: The cancellation error is swallowed so existing error propagation remains unchanged while the response body is released.

finding.title: Consecutive-cron-error escalation misses streaks interrupted by skipped_neutral runs
finding.description: loadCronHealth escalates a critical cron to the consecutive-error tier only when `runs[0].status === 'error' && runs[1].status === 'error'` (lines 602-609). But the enclosing latestErrorRunFresh condition (591-592) deliberately looks through skipped_neutral runs via latestRequiredCronRun, because shared-slot crons routinely interleave skipped_neutral rows between real attempts. A job whose real attempts are error, error but whose most recent row is skipped_neutral (or error/skipped_neutral/error) satisfies latestErrorRunFresh yet fails the raw runs[0]/runs[1] check, so a genuinely sustained failure is reported as a single transient — deriveAvailabilityStatus stays 'degraded' instead of 'stale'. The two code paths apply inconsistent skip-filtering to the same question.
finding.recommendation: Filter to required runs before the streak check: `const required = runs.filter(r => r.status !== 'skipped_neutral')` and test required[0]/required[1] === 'error'. This matches the documented intent ('two most-recent runs both in-error') under the same skip semantics the freshness logic already uses. Escalation-only change on an internal ops surface; verify against __tests__/cron-health.test.ts expectations first.
finding.estImpact: correct stale-escalation for shared-slot crons

accepted.notes: Mechanics confirmed: shared promise (lines 29-30), background cancel() (line 68), sync clone() (105/119); cancel-before-clone throws TypeError → 500 via withErrorHandler. But the race needs same-isolate concurrency in a seconds-wide window exactly as cache age crosses the 1-day boundary (or a vanished cache row) — sporadic and self-healing. Downgrade to low.

finding.title: Shared in-flight detail refresh: background body.cancel() races sync clone(), yielding 500s
finding.description: startStablecoinDetailRefresh de-dupes concurrent refreshes per coin by sharing ONE Promise<Response> (line 29-30). scheduleStablecoinDetailRefresh attaches `.then((response) => response.body?.cancel())` (line 68) to that shared promise. If a second request for the same coin arrives while that refresh is in flight and takes a synchronous path — cache age crossing DETAIL_STALE_CACHE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (= 1 day) at line 93, or the cache row vanishing — it receives the SAME promise and calls `response.clone()` (lines 105/119). When the background continuation was attached first, its cancel() disturbs the body before the sync caller resumes, and clone() on a disturbed body throws TypeError, which withErrorHandler converts to a 500 for a request that should have succeeded.
finding.recommendation: Make the shared in-flight value immune to consumer ordering: inside the shared promise, buffer the payload once (e.g. resolve to {status, headers, bodyText} or a fully-read Response) and have each consumer construct/clone its own Response; the scheduled path then needs no cancel() at all. This only removes the erroneous 500 in the race window; all successful responses are byte-identical.
finding.estImpact: eliminates sporadic 500s on /api/stablecoin/<id> under concurrency

remediation.summary: Changed shared stablecoin-detail refreshes to materialize response bytes and metadata once, then construct a fresh Response for each consumer so background refresh handling cannot disturb synchronous callers.
remediation.notes: Added a regression where a stale-cache background refresh and a synchronous cold-cache caller share the same in-flight refresh and both complete without cloning a disturbed body.

accepted.notes: Verified lines 676-684: both branches serve snapshot.payload with identical blacklistSummaryHeaders(freshnessTs), so the two-step equals one allowStale read and the TTL gate is observably dead. finding.title: handleBlacklistSummary reads the same snapshot row from D1 twice; the TTL check is dead logic
finding.description: Lines 676-684: the handler first calls readBlacklistSummarySnapshot(db, now) (TTL-gated), and on null immediately calls readBlacklistSummarySnapshot(db, now, {allowStale:true}) — an identical `SELECT value, updated_at FROM cache WHERE key = ?` for the same key. Both hits are served identically (same payload, same blacklistSummaryHeaders(freshnessTs)), so the two-step is exactly equivalent to a single allowStale read: whenever the snapshot exists and parses, it is served regardless of TTL. The BLACKLIST_SUMMARY_PRODUCER_SNAPSHOT_TTL_SEC gate therefore has zero observable effect, and every request where the producer snapshot is stale or missing pays a duplicate D1 round-trip.
finding.recommendation: Collapse to one readBlacklistSummarySnapshot(db, now, {allowStale:true}) call (and drop the now-unused TTL branch/param if nothing else uses it). Responses are provably identical in all cases, so this is safe under the freeze. If the original intent was 'rebuild inline when stale', that is NOT what ships today — flag to the owner before 'fixing' toward that intent, since it would change latency/behavior.

Same responses in all non-racy executions; the only delta is no longer catching a cache entry written milliseconds earlier, which the next request serves anyway.

accepted.notes: Verified: score.ts lacks tie expansion, watermark = max recorded_at seen; snapshot cron writes day-quantized snapshotDay so all daily rows tie; backfill with maxRows-only leaves since undefined so watermark advances. dews/yield/mint-burn have the expansion re-query; freeze/depeg do not. finding.title: Score projector watermark can permanently skip grade-change rows at LIMIT/tie boundaries
finding.description: projectScoreByVariant scans `safety_grade_history WHERE recorded_at > ? ... LIMIT ?` then advances the watermark to the max recorded_at seen. But recorded_at is day-quantized: snapshot-safety-grade-history.ts writes every row with `snapshotDay` (Math.floor(nowSec/DAY_SECONDS)*DAY_SECONDS), so ALL rows written in a day share one timestamp. If the batch limit cuts inside a tie group (multi-day catch-up after an outage, initial backfill, or an operator POST to /api/backfill-tape with only maxRows — since==null so the watermark IS advanced), the remaining same-timestamp rows are permanently skipped: next run filters `recorded_at > watermark`. freeze.ts (line 134) and depeg.ts (line 174) share the exact pattern with second-precision ties. dews.ts/yield.ts/mint-burn.ts already solve this with a tie-expansion re-query.
finding.recommendation: Apply the same tie-expansion used by dews/yield/mint-burn: when rows.length === limit, re-query unbounded with `recorded_at > since AND recorded_at <= cutoff` so the full tie group is processed before advancing the watermark (or advance only to the last fully-scanned timestamp). Safe under the freeze: in the normal non-truncated path output is byte-identical; the change only prevents silent event loss in the failure window.
finding.estImpact: prevents permanent tape-event loss on catch-up runs

remediation.summary: Added same-timestamp tie expansion to the score tape projector before advancing the grade-change watermark. A regression test now covers maxRows cutting through day-quantized safety grade rows so all rows at the cutoff timestamp are projected.

finding.title: DexScreener provider attaches the run-cumulative rejection map to per-batch diagnostics by reference
finding.description: buildDexScreenerQuotes increments the run-level `rejectedTargets` accumulator, and line 121 assigns that same object to `diagnostic.rejectionReasonCounts`. With more than one batch, every batch diagnostic would (a) report cumulative counts across all prior batches and (b) share one live object, so later batches retroactively mutate earlier diagnostics. This is dormant only because DEXSCREENER_ADDRESS_MAX_REQUESTS is currently 1; raising the cap (the constant exists precisely to be tuned) silently corrupts per-attempt telemetry. birdeye.ts (lines 64-98) already models the correct pattern with a separate per-request `requestRejectedTargets` map alongside the run accumulator.
finding.recommendation: Mirror birdeye: pass a fresh per-batch map into buildDexScreenerQuotes, copy its counts into both the batch diagnostic and the run-level rejectedTargets. Output-identical today (single batch, so per-batch == cumulative and no later mutation occurs); removes the landmine for any future cap increase.
finding.estImpact: hardens diagnostics against a 1-line constant change

remediation.summary: Split DexScreener address rejection accounting into run-level and batch-local maps, copying batch-local rejection counts into each diagnostic so diagnostics no longer alias the cumulative accumulator.
remediation.notes: Added a regression proving diagnostic rejection counts are a snapshot copy and do not mutate when the run-level rejectedTargets object changes later.

finding.title: Request-capped address providers silently drop remaining targets from telemetry
finding.description: dexscreener.ts and dexpaprika.ts emit buildCapSkipDiagnostic for targets beyond their request caps, so the pricing-provider diagnostics account for every candidate. The other four providers do not: moralis (MORALIS_ADDRESS_MAX_REQUESTS=3, inner-loop break leaves whole later chain groups unqueried and unreported), coingecko-onchain (cap 5, same pattern), alchemy (buildAlchemyBatches slices to 20 batches silently), and birdeye (slice(0,10) silently). Targets past the cap vanish: no diagnostic row, no rejection count, so status-side source-depth investigations under-count why coins lack quotes. Additionally moralis/coingecko-onchain keep iterating remaining chain groups after the cap purely to break immediately — noise, though not a correctness issue.
finding.recommendation: Compute processed-vs-total per provider and append the same buildCapSkipDiagnostic the DexScreener/DexPaprika paths use (label per provider). Purely additive diagnostic rows — quotes, ordering, and request counts are untouched, so runtime pricing behavior is identical; only the internal diagnostics stream gains previously-missing rows. Optionally break the outer group loop once the cap is hit.
finding.estImpact: complete cap accounting across all 6 providers

remediation.summary: Added additive request-cap diagnostics for Moralis, CoinGecko Onchain, Alchemy, and Birdeye address providers so targets skipped by provider request caps are visible in diagnostics without changing quote or request behavior.

finding.title: Brush drags fire a new /api/events fetch per pointer-move via raw-timestamp annotation query keys
finding.description: useChartAnnotations keys its query on the exact fromMs/toMs it receives ({coin, since, until}) and puts them in the fetch path. Its two live callers derive that window from the chart brush: ChartBrush calls onChange([lo, hi]) on every pointermove (sync.tsx:151-188), and use-market-data-chart-window.ts:34-36 / market-data-section.tsx feed the resulting float-millisecond bounds straight into the hook. Every pixel of a brush drag therefore mints a never-repeating query key and fires a fresh /api/events request (enabled=true, no debounce), leaving dozens of one-shot entries in the TanStack cache per drag. The memo at lines 131-176 already clamps annotations to the raw [lo, hi], so the fetch granularity is invisible to the rendered output.
finding.recommendation: Quantize since/until inside the hook before building the key/path (e.g. floor `since` to UTC day start, ceil `until` to day end) while keeping the memo's clamp on the raw fromMs/toMs; a whole brush drag then collapses to at most a handful of shared cache entries. Rendered pins are unchanged because clamping already happens client-side (only caveat: the server's 200-event limit; passing severityFloor=warning — the hook drops lower severities client-side anyway — more than compensates). Alternatively debounce the window fed to the hook.
finding.estImpact: removes ~30-100 redundant API fetches per brush interaction

remediation.summary: Bucketed chart-annotation /api/events query keys and paths into 30-day windows while preserving the existing raw [fromMs, toMs] clamp for rendered annotations, so brush pointer moves reuse cache entries instead of issuing a request per pixel.

finding.title: getNodePresentation computes hubLabelY that duplicates (and diverges from) labelY in ContagionGraphNode
finding.description: getNodePresentation computes `hubLabelY = clamp(position.y + node.r + (isCoreHub ? 12 : 10))` (line 208) while ContagionGraphNode independently computes `labelY = clamp(position.y + visualR + labelGap)` (lines 268-269) with the identical clamp and identical gap when `showTickerLabels` is false. The render picks `showTickerLabels ? labelY : hubLabelY` (line 379). The two are equal in every reachable case only because hub labels are suppressed whenever nodeScale ≠ 1 (contagion-graph-stage.tsx sets suppressHubLabels for detail presentation) — hubLabelY uses unscaled `node.r`, so the duplication is also a latent divergence trap if a future caller enables hub labels with scaling.
finding.recommendation: Delete `hubLabelY` from getNodePresentation and use the node-local `labelY` for both branches (`y={labelY}`); when showTickerLabels is false, labelGap already resolves to the same `isCoreHub ? 12 : 10` and visualR === node.r under the only nodeScale (1) where hub labels render. Output positions are numerically identical for all current callers.
finding.estImpact: -5 LOC, removes a scale-mismatch trap

remediation.summary: Removed the duplicated `hubLabelY` coordinate from contagion graph node presentation and rendered both ticker and hub labels from the single node-local `labelY` calculation.

accepted.notes: Verified end to end: worker buildPerCoinQuarterlyEventTypes emits sortKeyToLabel "Qn 'YY" labels; seismograph sorts them with localeCompare (line 68), so "Q1 '26" precedes "Q2 '17" — bars, NOTABLE_QUAKES pins, and ticks render non-chronologically whenever data spans years (it does). finding.title: FreezeWatch seismograph sorts quarters lexically, scrambling the timeline
finding.description: buildQuarterPoints() merges per-coin quarterly points keyed by the quarter LABEL and sorts with `a.localeCompare(b)`. Labels come from sortKeyToLabel() (shared/lib/blacklist-aggregates.ts:17) in the form "Qn 'YY" (e.g. "Q3 '22"), so lexical sort orders by quarter number before year: Q1 '17, Q1 '18, … Q1 '26, Q2 '17, … (verified by simulation). Blacklist data spans 2017→2026 across USDT/USDC/etc., so the SeismographSvg bars, the NOTABLE_QUAKES annotations (Tornado Cash/Silvergate/OFAC pins land at wrong x positions), and the sparse x-axis tick labels all render in scrambled, non-chronological order on /freezewatch/. Headline stats (peak quarter, totals) are unaffected since they are order-independent.
finding.recommendation: Sort chronologically by parsed (year, quarter) — e.g. derive key = (2000 + Number(label.slice(-2))) * 4 + Number(label[1]) — or better, have the worker payload carry the numeric quarter_sort_key alongside the label. This is a genuine correctness fix restoring the intended chronological rendering (behaviorChange flagged because pixels change).
finding.estImpact: fixes scrambled 10-year timeline chart on /freezewatch/

remediation.summary: Parsed FreezeWatch quarter labels into chronological year/quarter sort keys before rendering the seismograph, with focused coverage proving multi-year labels sort by time instead of lexically.

accepted.notes: Both claims verified: enrichment (line 189-193) only flags slices already 'direct' under the same context, and reserveSliceBlacklistRisk short-circuits on blacklistable===true, so the double regex pass is a no-op for classification. finding.title: Bulk blacklist resolution does redundant regex work: pointless slice enrichment + duplicate final convergence pass
finding.description: Two redundancies in the same resolver. (1) resolveBlacklistStatusWithoutExplicitOverride (lines 262-281) calls enrichReserveSlicesForBlacklist, then re-runs reserveSliceBlacklistRisk on every enriched slice. Enrichment only sets blacklistable=true on slices whose risk is already 'direct', and the loop's first check is slice.blacklistable === true — so enrichment can never change the loop's classification; every slice's regex battery (18 direct + 19 possible + 12 custody patterns + symbol matchers) runs twice. (2) resolveBlacklistStatuses (lines 339-348): when a pass adds no ids, blacklistableIds was unchanged for the whole pass, so the statuses just computed are already final — yet the code discards them and re-resolves all ~408 coins against an identical finalContext, a full extra O(coins × slices × patterns) pass. Variant coins additionally re-resolve their parent recursively each time.
finding.recommendation: In resolveBlacklistStatusWithoutExplicitOverride, delete the enrichedReserves computation and iterate effectiveReserves directly (enrichReserveSlicesForBlacklist stays for its real consumer, enrichLiveSlicesForBlacklist). In resolveBlacklistStatuses, accumulate the per-coin statuses into a Map during each pass and return that map when addedThisPass is false, instead of re-resolving. Both are provably behavior-identical: enrichment is a no-op for classification, and on the terminating pass the id set and symbol matchers never changed mid-pass.
finding.estImpact: ~2-3x less regex work per report-card build; -10 LOC

remediation.summary: Removed the no-op reserve-slice enrichment from the blacklist classification path and changed bulk blacklist resolution to return the statuses computed during the terminal convergence pass instead of re-resolving every coin against an unchanged final context. `enrichLiveSlicesForBlacklist` keeps the enrichment helper for its real live-slice consumer.

accepted.notes: Verified at yield-source.ts:123-131: comparator recomputes yieldSourceScore per comparison and tie-breaks recompute depth/freshness; engine.ts:176/247 invoke per coin. finding.title: selectYieldSource recomputes 4-factor source scores inside the sort comparator
finding.description: The candidates.sort comparator calls yieldSourceScore(b) and yieldSourceScore(a) — each running venue matching, excessApyConcave, depth log10 and freshness math — on every comparison, so each candidate's score is recomputed O(log n) times per sort, and depth/freshness scores are recomputed again in the later tie-break branches. The engine runs this per surviving coin per selector invocation. Numerically it also relies on recomputation being bit-identical (true today, but fragile if any sub-score gains caching or randomness).
finding.recommendation: Precompute `{candidate, score, risk, depth, freshness}` once per candidate (a Schwartzian transform), then sort on the cached fields. Identical comparison values, so ordering and output are unchanged; strictly behavior-preserving and slightly simpler to read.
finding.estImpact: ~5x fewer score evaluations per yield-source selection

finding.title: Inconsistent sort comparator in depeg-history projection risks nondeterministic dataset output
finding.description: projectDepegHistory sorts with `(a, b) => (b.startedAtISO > a.startedAtISO ? 1 : -1)`. For two rows with equal startedAtISO (two coins depegging in the same second — plausible in correlated events), compare(a,b) and compare(b,a) both return -1, an inconsistent comparator whose result ordering is implementation-defined. Since the emitted latest/dated CSV/JSON/NDJSON artifacts are committed and diffed byte-for-byte (writeArtifact change detection, check mode), an order flip between runs causes spurious artifact churn in the dated depeg-history mirrors.
finding.recommendation: Use a total order with a deterministic tiebreak, e.g. `b.startedAtISO.localeCompare(a.startedAtISO) || a.id - b.id` (rows carry the numeric event id). For all current non-tied data the output is identical; ties get a stable, defined order instead of an undefined one.
finding.estImpact: eliminates spurious dataset-artifact churn on tied events

finding.title: Picker 'current-deviation' context key never fires for below-peg coins (missing Math.abs)
finding.description: deriveContextKeys() pushes the 'current-deviation' context key when `row.currentDeviationBps != null && row.currentDeviationBps > 25`. currentDeviationBps is signed: worker/src/lib/depeg-signals.ts computes bps = (price/pegRef - 1) * 10000, so below-peg coins carry NEGATIVE values, and the selector data adapter (src/app/screener/picker/selector-data-adapter.ts:86) passes that value through. A coin trading 100 bps BELOW peg (the risky direction) therefore never gets the context key, while a 26 bps premium does. Every sibling consumer uses abs: exclusions.ts:159 uses Math.abs(row.currentDeviationBps), and what-to-watch-templates.ts renderWatchText uses roundedBps() = Math.round(Math.abs(...)) >= 25 for the very same threshold — strong evidence the signed comparison is an oversight, not a deliberate above-only rule.
finding.recommendation: Change the guard to `Math.abs(row.currentDeviationBps) > 25`. This is a one-token computation-bug fix; it adds the 'current-deviation' context key (and downstream chips/snapshot contextKeys) for below-peg coins, so it is behavior-changing but corrects output that is currently wrong in the direction that matters most.

finding.title: compareScored is a non-transitive comparator passed to Array.sort
finding.description: compareScored returns score order only when |scoreA − scoreB| > 1.5, otherwise falls through to supply/grade/liquidity tie-breaks. This violates transitivity: e.g. A(score 100, supply 1), B(98.6, 100), C(97.2, 200) gives B>A (window, supply), C>B (window, supply), but A>C (2.8 > 1.5) — a cycle. Array.prototype.sort with an inconsistent comparator produces implementation-defined order; today's output is only deterministic because the input order into sort is deterministic, so any upstream reordering (or a JS-engine algorithm change) can silently reshuffle picker ranks near the window boundary. The same windowed-threshold comparator pattern recurs in yield-source.ts:123 (0.0001 epsilon, practically harmless).
finding.recommendation: Do not fix by naively changing sort semantics (that would move ranks, violating the freeze). Instead document the invariant and pin it: compute a total order explicitly (e.g. bucket scores into 1.5-wide clusters first, then tie-break within clusters), verified to reproduce current output on the live universe before swapping. At minimum add a comment warning that ranked order depends on input order.
finding.estImpact: removes implementation-defined ordering risk in picker ranks

remediation.summary: Replaced the non-transitive selector ranking comparator with a score-first total comparator and explicit 1.5-point score clusters before applying tie-breakers. finding.title: Lease renewal conflates transient D1 errors with definitive ownership loss, and has no overload retry
finding.description: In runCronWithLease, lease acquisition (line 220) and release (line 354) are wrapped in runWithOverloadRetry, but the heartbeat renewal (line 249) is not. markLeaseFailure (238-245) counts a thrown transient D1 overload error identically to renewed=false (a definitive ownership transfer, which can only happen after the TTL expired and another owner won the upsert). Consequences: (a) maxRenewFailures consecutive D1 hiccups (2 by default; 3 at 30s spacing for LONG_RUNNING jobs per handlers/scheduled/context.ts:30) abort a healthy 8-13 minute cron with CronLeaseLostError while its lease is still validly held; (b) after a provable ownership loss, the job keeps writing for up to (maxRenewFailures-1)*heartbeatSec more before aborting, extending the dual-writer window the lease exists to prevent.
finding.recommendation: Wrap renewCronLeaseState in runWithOverloadRetry(fn, 2) like acquire/release, and in the .then handler abort immediately (leaseLost=true, leaseController.abort) when renewal returns renewed=false, reserving the maxRenewFailures counter for thrown errors only. Internal coordination only — no API shapes, figures, or cron result formats change; the fix strictly narrows both failure windows.
finding.estImpact: removes spurious long-cron aborts; shrinks dual-writer window by up to 60s

remediation.summary: Wrapped lease heartbeats in overload retry, made definitive renewal ownership loss abort immediately, and reserved the max-renew-failures counter for thrown renewal errors. finding.title: Idempotency PENDING reservations never expire — a killed isolate poisons the key with 409s for up to 7 days
finding.description: runIdempotentAdminAction reserves the key with response_status=-1 (PENDING), then runs execute(). Every failure path that runs code cleans up, but if the isolate dies mid-execute (Cloudflare wall-clock kill — plausible for 'trigger-digest' in admin-actions.ts:24, which runs a multi-minute digest inline — eviction, or crash), the PENDING row survives with no TTL. All subsequent retries with the same key hit line 112 (existing PENDING, insertedReservation=false) and get 409 'Idempotency key is currently in progress'. The only cleanup is the 7-day created_at prune at line 244, which itself only runs on the success path of some other keyed request. The client's documented recovery ('retry with a new Idempotency-Key') is only messaged for the FAILED state, not this one.
finding.recommendation: Treat PENDING rows older than a bounded max execution time (e.g., 20 min > any admin action) as abandoned: before returning the 409, attempt a single-statement takeover UPDATE ... SET request_hash=?, created_at=? WHERE action=? AND idempotency_key=? AND response_status=-1 AND created_at<? and proceed as the reservation owner if changes>0. Normal-path responses are byte-identical; only the currently-wedged state changes (from a permanent 409 to a working retry).

finding.description: The comment (lines 6-8) says app timeouts stay below the platform wall-clock limit so a controlled error row is logged instead of losing the invocation. But slot chains run jobs sequentially, each with its own full CRON_TIMEOUT_MS and no shared deadline (run-best-effort-job.ts / context.ts pass no slot budget into runLeasedCron). Worst-case chain budgets: quarterHourly 33 min (5+8+5+5+5+5), fourHourlyReserveSync 27 min (12+5+5+5), fiveMinuteTelegram 29 min, daily-0805 digest chain 26 min (14+12). unverified.title: _routes.json routes fonts, chain icons, feeds, and other static assets through Pages Functions for nothing
unverified.description: The exclude list covers /logos/*, /dexes/*, /featured/*, /maps/*, /datasets/*, /postman/*, /og-*.png — but misses /fonts/* (6 woff2 files, ~250KB, fetched on every cold page view via globals.css), /chains/* (102 icons, 2.4MB, rendered in bulk on chain/table pages), /icons/*, /sheets/*.csv, /feed/*.xml, /critical-css-loader.js (loaded on the homepage), and root images (pharos-icon.*, tokenbrice.png, claude.png, apple-touch-icon.png, favicon-800*.png). Every such request invokes functions/_middleware.ts, which for non-HTML responses passes through completely untouched (injectHtmlCsp returns non-HTML unchanged, csp-inject.ts:27), so the invocation is pure overhead: it burns Pages Functions request quota and adds latency versus direct asset serving.
unverified.recommendation: Add "/fonts/*", "/chains/*", "/icons/*", "/sheets/*", "/feed/*", "/critical-css-loader.js", and the static root images to the exclude array (well under the 100-rule limit). Behavior-preserving: the middleware provably does nothing to these responses, and _headers rules apply to directly-served assets regardless.
unverified.estImpact: eliminates ~10+ no-op Function invocations per cold page view

unverified.title: /logos/* cached 1y immutable while logo files are replaced in place under the same name
unverified.description: public/_headers serves /logos/* with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, but logo URLs are not content-addressed: commit a19c76621 (2026-06-10) modified 30+ existing files in place (295-usdaf.png, 50-eurc.png, busd0-usual.png, ...), and scripts/maintenance/fetch-logos.ts and generate-compact-logos.mjs both overwrite files at fixed names. Any browser that fetched a logo before a replacement will render the stale artwork for up to a year, and `immutable` tells the browser to never revalidate even on reload. Chains/dexes/featured deliberately use max-age=604800 for the same class of asset — /logos/* is the outlier.
unverified.recommendation: Change the /logos/* rule to `public, max-age=604800, immutable` (matching /chains/*), or drop `immutable`. Config-only header change, no product figures or page content affected; correctness improves after future logo replacements.
unverified.estImpact: stale-logo window drops from 1 year to 7 days

unverified.title: manifest.webmanifest and public/icons/ ship on every deploy but nothing links them since the manifest metadata was removed
unverified.description: Commit 70bbb0938 ('chore: trim root metadata request', 2026-06-07) deleted `manifest: "/manifest.webmanifest"` from src/app/layout.tsx to save one request. The manifest and its 5 icon files (public/icons/, 190KB, including the never-served icon-maskable-source.svg) still ship in every deploy but are referenced by zero pages — verified against live homepage HTML (no <link rel="manifest">). Without the link the manifest is functionally dead: no PWA installability, no maskable icons, nothing consumes /icons/*. The repo is carrying both halves of a contradiction: the PWA assets from 4410efa23 and the de-linking from 70bbb0938.
unverified.recommendation: Owner decision: if the trimmed-request tradeoff stands, delete public/manifest.webmanifest and public/icons/ (dead weight, zero behavior change since they are unreachable); if PWA install matters, restore the one-line `manifest:` field in layout metadata. Either resolution is one small change.
unverified.estImpact: -6 files / ~191KB per deploy, or restores PWA install

unverified.description: og-selector-trading.png, og-selector-treasury.png, og-selector-yield.png (277KB total) have zero references — the picker page only uses og-selector-default.png (src/app/screener/picker/page.tsx:12); the persona-specific cards were dropped in b1788bd0e ('fix(selector): secure snapshot sharing'). unverified.title: Committed dataset/depeg mirrors are 7 weeks stale and the --check row floors (1) would accept near-empty output
unverified.description: The checked-in mirrors are frozen at 2026-05-16 ('safety-score v7.25', 547 rows) while live prod serves asOf 2026-07-02, 'safety-score v8.13', 555 rows; data/depeg-events.json still holds only the single seeded USDC event from May 20. Production is protected (PUBLIC_DATASETS_REQUIRE_API=1 regenerates before build), so this only degrades local/PR preview builds: JSON-LD dateModified/methodology baked from the stale import (analytics-dataset-json-ld.ts:3-6), and /depeg/[event] generateStaticParams builds exactly one event page. Additionally ROW_FLOORS in generate-public-datasets.ts:63 is 1 for every topic, so --check would bless a truncated 1-row mirror — the freshness/completeness of these committed artifacts is effectively unguarded.
unverified.recommendation: Refresh the committed mirrors on a cadence (one `npm run generate:public-datasets` + sync-depeg-events run against prod API, committed), and raise ROW_FLOORS to realistic minimums (e.g. top-stablecoins ≥300, scores-latest ≥300) so a silently truncated mirror fails the existence check. No production behavior changes; preview builds get representative data.
